data.body:
CANARY COUNTS — the anti-vacuous-green oracle, now read from the completed run rather than inferred.

Earlier I recorded the three arms as green but flagged the canary figures as still owed, because GitHub
serves no logs until a run fully completes. They are now retrieved from run 30846201728 (head d4095763e,
verified to contain the fix):
    anthropic  [llm-live-canary] collected=15 executed=14 skipped=1   -> 14 passed  (416.55s)
    bedrock    [llm-live-canary] collected=15 executed=15 skipped=0   -> 15 passed  (402.72s)
    openai     [llm-live-canary] collected=15 executed=14 skipped=1   -> 14 passed  (150.32s)
Every arm EXECUTED live tests; the bedrock arm skipped nothing at all. The single skip on the anthropic and
openai arms is `test_bedrock_arm_resolved_a_region`, which pytest.skips with "region resolution is a
Bedrock-arm concern" — legitimate and identical on both, so it is not an arm-specific silent skip.
This is the direct oracle for AC4: a green job conclusion could in principle sit on top of an all-skip, and
these counts exclude that.

ALSO LANDED: Gerrit 1315 (`f124: cite the ticket in unscanned files`). My leak-fix commit had embedded the
raw CI run id in seven comments; another session fixed the two .py files as 36e986c188, which is what
un-redded main, and 1315 is the rebased remainder covering the three provider overlays and the
review_skeleton example. WORTH KNOWING FOR WHOEVER OWNS THE GATE: check_comment_hygiene.py only scans
Python, so a rot-prone reference in .toml or workflow .yaml is invisible to it — which is exactly why those
four survived a green gate. That is a coverage gap, not a rule change.
